analytical_results.name: Uniform-q Potts exact-edge entropy bound, both signs
analytical_results.scope: Every finite simple G whose every edge has an endpoint of degree at most3. Uniform q-color singleton law; common Potts table lambda_s with diagonal s/q and off-diagonal(1-s)/(q(q-1)), s in[0,1]. For s<1/q additionally require G bipartite; for s>=1/q no bipartiteness is needed. All actual bipartite K4 subdivisions are covered. The q=1 case is trivial.
analytical_results.conclusion: There is an actual joint law with every singleton and every edge table exact and KL at most m I_q(s), where I_q(s)=s log(qs)+(1-s)log(q(1-s)/(q-1)). No exchangeable triple extension is needed as a proof premise; the input triple-feasibility restrictions remain separate.

checked_route_obstructions: Naively specifying branch correlations by six stationary path powers can demand a negative variance even for a legitimate binary triple input. This defeats that branch-gluing rule, not the exact-edge entropy target.
One shared exchangeable triple-orbit latent variable does not preserve IID edge constraints globally. A full-support multistate C4 example also defeats naive incident-matrix identifiability.

A strictly positive three-state triple-extendible pair table defeats separately sharp quotient-first binary-indicator budgeting: its quotient pair is independent, but every full-table joint needs correlated global indicators. Cross-layer entropy transfer is essential. The full entropy target is not refuted.

Actual Markov-square examples have negative individual centered full terms or spectral prefix summands. Proper-subgraph/constant-mode surplus cannot be discarded; failed modewise positivity is not a counterexample to the full density.
Six different nonnegative PSD Markov kernels can commute and still give colored density1-t^6/16<1. They are not powers of one host. This refutes a multiple-base cone shortcut but not target B.
For three distinct centered spectral levels, A and A^2 cannot generally share a one-base affine cone of the preceding form. Truncated spectral projection kernels need not be entrywise nonnegative.

feasibility_clarification.statement: For every strictly positive compatible symmetric pair table on a finite bipartite G, exact full-support joint feasibility is easy; the unresolved issue is its sharp entropy budget, not the existence of some exact marginal fit.
feasibility_clarification.argument: Choose0<epsilon<min(1,min_xy lambda_xy/(kappa_x kappa_y)) and lambda'=(lambda-epsilon kappa^2)/(1-epsilon). Broadcast the two coordinates of one lambda' pair to the two bipartition classes, then mix this law with epsilon times the IID kappa^V law. Each actual edge and singleton is exactly the target, and every configuration has positive mass. This alone supplies no sharp KL estimate.

exact_remaining_obligations.B: Dominate the collective mixed-band commutator/negative-prefix contribution using the available cycle, diamond and constant-mode surplus on general actual common-power hosts. The still-uncovered regime includes three or more interacting centered spectral levels outside previously proved mixing/reflection criteria. Per-mode positivity and independently colored PSD kernels cannot replace this obligation.
